intro.title: Build typed theme contract checker
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed theme contract checker, a tool that validates if a given theme object matches a predefined structure. You'll learn how to use TypeScript interfaces to define a strict contract for your theme's shape, ensuring type safety. The core concept involves creating a validation function that checks an object against this interface, using type guards and conditional logic. This project will help you understand how TypeScript's static typing can prevent runtime errors and improve code reliability in real-world applications.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for maintaining consistent theming across large-scale applications like design systems, admin dashboards, and enterprise software. For example, when building a dashboard with multiple panels, modals, and data visualizations, developers need to ensure all components use valid theme values like colors, spacing, and typography. A typed theme contract checker prevents UI inconsistencies by catching invalid theme references during development, such as using a non-existent color in a button component or an incorrect spacing token in a card layout. This approach is commonly used in products like Figma's design system, Shopify's admin interface, and Microsoft's Fluent UI to maintain visual coherence across complex interfaces.
